native_result.query: The effect of which variable on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024 to 0.0923 (while becoming insignifcant) when both SES and academic characteristics are included in analysis?
native_result.HypoA: The effect of SES on BA degree completion decreases from 0.3636  (significant) to  -0.2293 (insignificant) and effect of race on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024  (significant) to 0.0923 (insignificant) when academic characteristics are considered.
native_result.HypoB: Эффект переменной SAMPLE_RACE (расового разрыва «не-белые против белых», прежде всего Black vs White, с тем же паттерном у Hispanic) на завершение BA сокращается с большой значимой величины до примерно 0.09 и становится статистически незначимым, когда в логистическую регрессию BA DEGREE COMPLETED одновременно включаются SES и академические характеристики (ABILITY: COMPOSITE OF ASVAB SCORE и PERCENTILE IN CLASS): в основной спецификации |b| 0.5801/0.4846 (p=0.005/0.049) переходят к 0.5168/0.2887 (p=0.023/0.268), а в спецификации без контроля размера семьи разрыв Black сжимается с 1.0057 (p=8e-7) до 0.0926 (p=0.68), теряя 90.8% величины. Механизм — полная медиация: расовая принадлежность смещена относительно ресурсов и школьных достижений (r(Black, ASVAB)=-0.36, r(Black, SES)=-0.15, r(Hispanic, SES)=-0.25), а эти признаки сильно предсказывают BA (LR chi2=276, 2 df, p=1e-60 для академического блока), поэтому после условия на них остаточный расовый эффект неотличим от нуля. Альтернативы отвергаются: FAMILY SIZE OF SAMPLE не уменьшается (-0.4865 -> -0.5248, p<1e-16), SAMPLE_SEX не уменьшается и незначим в обеих моделях (0.2340 -> 0.2654, p 0.082 -> 0.065).

sub_hypo.text: Adjustment for socioeconomic status and academic characteristics attenuates racial differences in BA completion. Main binomial logistic regression of BA completion, using raw log-odds, White and Male reference categories, and controls for sex and family size.
sub_hypo.relations: Adding SES and academic characteristics reduces the absolute Black-versus-White and Hispanic-versus-White log-odds coefficients; only the Hispanic coefficient becomes statistically nonsignificant in the reported main specification.

sub_hypo.text: Without controlling for family size, adjustment for SES and academic characteristics reduces the absolute Black-versus-White BA-completion coefficient from 1.0057 (p=8e-7) to 0.0926 (p=0.68), a 90.8% reduction that renders the residual racial effect statistically indistinguishable from zero.
sub_hypo.context: NLS participants; auxiliary logistic-regression specification excluding family-size control, distinguished from the main specification.
sub_hypo.relations: SES and academic adjustment attenuates the Black-versus-White coefficient by 90.8% to approximately 0.09 and removes statistical significance in the specification without family-size control.

sub_hypo.text: The proposed mechanism is full mediation through socioeconomic resources and academic achievement: Black status correlates negatively with ASVAB ability (r=-0.36) and SES (r=-0.15), and Hispanic status correlates negatively with SES (r=-0.25). SES and academic characteristics predict BA completion, with a strong joint contribution from the academic block (LR chi-square=276, 2 df, p=1e-60).
sub_hypo.context: NLS participants; nested logistic models adding SES and the academic block to background predictors. Full mediation is the proposed interpretation, although the reported main specification retains a significant Black coefficient.
sub_hypo.relations: Race is associated with socioeconomic resources and academic achievement, which predict BA completion; conditioning on these proposed mediators is hypothesized to eliminate the residual racial association.

sub_hypo.text: Family size does not exhibit the hypothesized attenuation: its BA-completion coefficient changes from -0.4865 to -0.5248 and remains significant at p<1e-16.
sub_hypo.context: NLS participants; comparison of baseline and fully adjusted main logistic models, with SES and academic characteristics added.
sub_hypo.relations: The negative family-size association increases in absolute magnitude after adjustment rather than attenuating, rejecting family size as an alternative example of the proposed mediation pattern.

sub_hypo.text: Sex does not exhibit the hypothesized attenuation: the Female-versus-Male BA-completion coefficient increases from 0.2340 to 0.2654, while remaining statistically nonsignificant (p=0.082 to 0.065).
sub_hypo.context: NLS participants; comparison of baseline and fully adjusted main logistic models, using Male as the sex reference category.
sub_hypo.relations: The sex coefficient increases rather than attenuates after SES and academic adjustment and is nonsignificant in both models, rejecting sex as an alternative example of the proposed mediation pattern.
